title: Ghanaian Okro Soup
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: Finely diced rather than puréed, dry-fried three minutes, then stock and half a teaspoon of edible potash — and seven kinds of seafood.
longDesc: The other way to make Ewe okra soup, and it is the opposite of the dough method: five hundred grams of okra finely diced and dry-fried for three minutes, then stock for two minutes, then half a teaspoon of edible potash or a teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda for one minute more. The seafood load is extraordinary — grilled mackerel, smoked haddock, cubed salmon, cod, crabs, smoked tilapia and prawns, plus shiitake mushrooms. Three tablespoons of zomi, a litre of fish stock and three hundred grams of kale or spinach. She calls it homage to her Ewe dish of banku and okra soup.
ingredients: 3 tbsp zomi (spiced palm oil), or groundnut oil
1/2 tsp edible potash, or 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda
steps: Soften the onion in the zomi, about 2 minutes.
Add the chilli and cook 2 minutes.
Add the blended ginger and cook 3 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Add the smoked tilapia and cook 5 minutes.
Separately dry-fry the finely diced okra 3 minutes.
Add stock to the okra and cook 2 minutes.
Add the edible potash or bicarbonate of soda and cook for another minute.
Combine with the soup base and cook 2 minutes.
Add the remaining seafood, the mushrooms and the greens, and let it steam 5 minutes.
chefTips: Dry-frying the diced okra for three minutes before any liquid is the move that distinguishes this version. It drives off some water and concentrates the flavour before the mucilage develops.
Half a teaspoon of edible potash OR a teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda — note the alkali is optional in effect but doubles in quantity if you switch. Potash is stronger.
The alkali goes in for ONE minute only, after the stock. Any longer and it will taste soapy.
Finely diced, not puréed. This gives a soup with recognisable okra in it rather than the self-bound dough of the other documented version.
Zomi is the deeper, spiced palm oil and only three tablespoons of it for eight servings — a lean soup by Ghanaian standards.
Seven kinds of seafood is a diaspora abundance rather than a village pot, and she is open that this is a UK adaptation. Use three or four and it will still work.
Kale as an alternative to spinach is her substitution and it holds its texture better in a long soup.
commonMistakes: Skipping the dry-fry and adding the okra to liquid.
Leaving the alkali in for more than a minute.
Swapping potash for soda at the same quantity.
Puréeing the okra, which belongs to the other version.
sources: Adapted from 'Ghanaian Okro Soup', ndudu-by-fafa.blogspot.com, byline as printed 'Posted by Fafa Gilbert', Wednesday 26 July 2017. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).
THE EWE CLAIM, quoted: 'Paying homage to my tribal, Ewe dish of Banku and Okra soup (traditionally known as Akple and Fetri Detchi).' Note the spelling 'Fetri Detchi' against 'fetri detsi' elsewhere.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 500g of finely diced Okra; 2 large finely diced Onions; 1 large roughly chopped onions; 50g of blended Ginger; 3 tablespoonfuls of Zomi (spiced Palm oil) or Groundnut oil; 2 Habanero chillies; Half a teaspoon of edible potash or 1 teaspoon of bicarbonate soda; 1 litre of Fish stock or Vegetable stock; 1 Shrimp stock cube; '300g of Kale of Spinach' — printed exactly like that, with 'of' where 'or' is meant; 3 large blended tomatoes; Salt and pepper to taste; plus 150g of Shitake Mushrooms, 2 large grilled Mackerel, 150g of smoked Haddock, 150g of cubed Salmon, 150g of cubed Cod, 200g of shelled medium sized crabs, 150g of smoked Tilapia, 150g of Prawns.

Step times as printed: onion 2 min, chilli 2 min, ginger 3 min, tomatoes 3 min, tilapia 5 min; okra dry-fried 3 min, stock 2 min, potash or soda 'Cook for another minute'; 'Cook for 2 minutes'; 'let it steam for 5 minutes'.
NO SENSORY DONENESS CUE is printed anywhere — only the step times. That absence is recorded.

AN AUTHOR-DECLARED UK ADAPTATION: smoked haddock, cod, salmon and shiitake mushrooms are not Ghanaian ingredients and the seven-seafood abundance is a diaspora construction. Flagged rather than removed.

THE FUNDAMENTAL DISAGREEMENT WITH THE OTHER DOCUMENTED EWE OKRA SOUP, unreconciled: SHE DICES the okra and cooks it in stock with an alkali; FRAN OSSEO-ASARE purées okra with onion and water into a self-binding 'mucilaginous dough' with no alkali at all (GHA088). Those are two different techniques producing two different textures, both published as fetri detsi by Ewe-connected cooks. Neither is corrected.

ON THE ALKALI: this is the only documented Ghanaian okra soup to use one. Edible potash in Ghana is the same family of mineral alkali as Nigeria's kaun, which is chemically trona rather than true potash.
ON ZOMI: palm oil processed further than ordinary red palm oil, darker and more strongly flavoured. See GHA028 and GHA034, where it is also specified by name.
storage: 2 days refrigerated. The seafood does not keep longer.
healthBenefits: Okra supplies soluble fibre, folate and vitamins C and K.
A very high and varied seafood load gives omega-3 fats, iodine, selenium and complete protein.
Kale or spinach adds vitamin A, vitamin K and iron.
Only three tablespoons of oil across eight servings.
culturalNote: Two Ewe-connected cooks publishing fundamentally different okra techniques under the same dish name is a good reminder that regional cuisines are not single recipes. The dicing-and-alkali route gives a soup you can see the okra in; the dough route gives something smoother and stranger. Both go with banku.
